Your best bet, IMHO, would be to piece the rifle together from scratch. This way it forces you to learn about the guns form, function, and even a little bit of history. That would be your cheapest, albeit most time consuming route.

The AR15 is comprised of about a hundred or so different parts. But when assembled, the gun can be quickly broken down into two main components; the upper receiver assembly, and the lower receiver assembly. Next on the "affordability" list would be to purchase the rifle in "halves."

http://www.midwayusa.com/product/241847/bushmaster-ar-15-patrolman-m4-a3-upper-receiver-assembly-556x45mm-nato-16-barrel?cm_vc=ProductFinding

Here you have a "flat top" upper receiver with a removable carry handle. The carry handle also houses your rear sight. The barrel is 16" long, which is the shortest length barrel a civilian can legally own without an NFA stamp from the BATFE. The barrel is also considered to have a "government profile" or "contour", which can be seen with the cutout in the barrel after the handguards. This cutout is for the military attachment of the M203 grenade launcher, which hasnt quite made ita way to the civilian market just yet. The barrel is also equipped with a permanent iron front sight base, which would be ideal on the battlefield. It is chambered in 5.56NATO, which will shoot 5.56 and .223 Remington. It is equipped with a carbine length gas system, which will reliably cycle cheap ammunition, as well as fire in the most demanding of conditions (READ: sandy, dirty, optimum choice gas system for the battlefield for reliable cycling of the weapon) For $400, you get a lot of bang for your buck in such a small package. (No pun intended) And that's just the upper assembly. Next you need to choose a plan for the lower assembly. For example, here we have a Stag Arms complete lower assembly for $278.

http://www.cheaperthandirt.com/product/3-0129059?td_source=search

It comes complete with the lower receiver, buffer tube, 6 position adjustable buttstock, fire control group, pistol grip, etc. Or you can go the "bare" or "stripped" route.

http://palmettostatearmory.com/index.php/catalog/product/view/id/10445/

Here you have a stripped lower receiver and you get to choose what parts and pieces you want. Keep in mind that the lower receiver is the "serialized" portion of the weapon and if purchased online would need to be transferred to an FFL (federally licensed firearm dealer eg. Your local gun shop) Most dealers charge a transfer fee as well.

I know this sounds like a lot, but my best advise is to educate yourself first before dumping hundreds, if not thousands of dollars into an AR15 that you're just going to strip everything off to upgrade with bits that you like. Just build what you want from the get go, and that will be your cheapest route. Best of luck on your AR journey.

As for attaining sub MOA groups @200 yards, build yourself an affordable rifle that you can afford to shoot often, and please do so...just practice practice practice. A particular rifle isn't going to make you a better shot.
